bear_case: The holiday tape's constructive readings — ES at 7,555, Europe records, NVDA's $200.06 touch — all occurred in thin, low-participation markets. The same force driving the bull case (57K NFP = rate cuts) also signals the US economy is deteriorating faster than the soft-landing consensus acknowledges. At Nasdaq P/E ~28x, simultaneous slowing growth and sticky June CPI (July 14 — energy-CPI base effects from Iranian oil normalization may not appear until July data; Cleveland Fed nowcasts remain elevated) creates a stagflation scenario where rate-cut and growth narratives contradict each other. Holiday-tape ES at 7,555 reflects an absence of sellers, not a presence of committed buyers — when those sellers return on July 6 with the 57K growth scare fresh, the gap-up becomes the distribution zone, not the re-entry zone. If SPX reclaims 7,460 on July 6 and holds, the bear case is wrong.
